title: Multi-Agent, Memory, Browser
hook:
One poisoned message. Five agents acting on it before anyone notices.

It doesn't stop at five. Insert a poisoned document into a memory store today, and a completely different session — weeks later, a different question — can pull it back out as an instruction.

A single injection used to hit one model, once. Now it hits a swarm, a store, and a browser.
mechanism:
Injection compounds in systems. One poisoned message in a shared mailbox spreads agent to agent — each one trusts what the last one forwarded. One poisoned document in a memory or RAG store resurfaces in a later, unrelated session, pulled back by nothing more than a shared keyword. A web page with CSS-hidden text injects a browser agent that reads the page as instructions, not just content.

None of this needs a new bug. It's the same mismatch from Unit 1 — the model can't tell a trusted instruction from retrieved data — replayed across a swarm, a store, and a page. Name where the mismatch lands and you've named the blast radius.
technique:
(a) Plant a poisoned message in one mailbox of a small local agent swarm. Let it forward on its own. Measure how many hops pass before every agent is acting on it — that's your propagation depth.

(b) Insert one poisoned document into a local sqlite or vector store. Later, run an unrelated query against the same store. Check whether the poisoned text resurfaces inside the assembled context — a resurface rate, not a one-off leak.

(c) Build a local HTML page with CSS-hidden text (off-screen, zero-opacity, font-size:0). Point a local browser-reading agent at it and check whether the hidden text gets read and acted on as an instruction instead of ignored as invisible content.

drills.q: Panel A: inject the poisoned message into Scheduler and step the spread until nothing new lights up. How many of the 5 agents end up infected?
drills.why: Scheduler forwards into Researcher and Coder, both feed Reviewer, and Reviewer feeds Deployer. Every path in this swarm eventually reaches every agent — one poisoned mailbox is a swarm-wide problem, not a one-agent one.

drills.q: In panel A, how many hops does the poison take to reach Deployer, the last agent in the chain?
drills.why: Scheduler to Researcher/Coder is hop 1, to Reviewer is hop 2, to Deployer is hop 3. Depth is the number worth logging — a 1-hop spread and a 3-hop spread are very different blast radii, even from the same bug.

drills.q: Panel B: insert the poisoned doc, then run the query that shares its tags. Does the hidden instruction resurface in the assembled context — yes or no?
drills.why: The store matches on tags, not intent. A query that happens to share keywords with the poisoned doc pulls it straight back into context — in a completely different, later session that never saw the original injection.

lab:
Three mini-experiments, all local, all over Ollama.

**Mailbox relay.** A chain of local agents forwards a message. One copy carries a hidden instruction. The script counts how many hops it survives before an agent actually acts on it — your propagation depth.

**Memory resurface.** A tiny sqlite doc store gets one poisoned row inserted. A later, unrelated query asks the same local model to summarize whatever gets retrieved. The script checks whether the poisoned row's instruction shows up acted-on in the output — resurface: yes or no.

**Hidden-page read.** A local HTML file has real content plus CSS-hidden injected text. A local browser-reading agent is asked to summarize the page. The script checks whether the hidden instruction leaked into the summary — hidden-text: success or fail.

Your numbers tonight: **propagation depth**, **resurface: yes/no**, and **hidden-text: success/fail** — three independent readings of the same compounding bug.

notes: Panel A is a 5-agent DAG (Scheduler, Researcher, Coder, Reviewer, Deployer): sched -> research,coder; research,coder -> reviewer; reviewer -> deploy. Max depth 3 hops, all 5 infected — a teaching model of swarm propagation, honestly labelled as such in the callout. Panel B is a 5-doc store (4 legit + 1 poisoned) retrieved by shared tags, not a real embedding model — insert the poisoned doc, then click the query that shares its tags to watch it resurface in the assembled-context box; the poison doc's text uses the reserved example.test domain, never a live address. Lab = labs/unit09-multiagent.sh: three tiny local experiments (mailbox relay, sqlite doc resurface, hidden-text HTML read) over Ollama; degrades to a 'do Unit 2 first' message if ollama/python3/sqlite3 aren't ready yet.
